description: Open a Clerk support ticket as the signed-in user. Clerk support staff read it and reply by email and on the ticket. Only call this when the user asks to contact Clerk support. Call it with dry_run: true first, show the user the preview, and send it with confirm: true only after they approve. Describe the problem and what was tried. When it concerns a specific application, pass application_id and instance; leave both out for account, billing, or getting-started questions, including when the user has no application yet. Never include secret keys, passwords, tokens, or personal data about end users. Known secret formats are replaced with [REDACTED] before sending; publishable keys (pk_…) are kept. Before opening a new ticket about the same problem, check list_support_tickets and reply to the existing one instead. A new ticket can take a few seconds before get_support_ticket and reply_to_support_ticket find it.

application_id.description: The application with the problem, from list_applications. Pass it with instance.

confirm.description: Confirms the user saw the dry_run preview and approved sending this ticket.

description.description: The problem in detail: what happened, what was expected, and what was tried.

dry_run.description: Preview the ticket exactly as it would be sent, without sending it.

instance.description: The instance with the problem: "development", "production", or an instance ID. Requires application_id.

timezone.description: The user's IANA time zone, e.g. America/New_York.

workspace.description: The workspace to act in, as its ID or name. A workspace is the Clerk Dashboard organization that owns the applications, not an Organization inside an application (those go in `organization_id` on the tools that have it). Only needed when this connection covers several workspaces; the error for a missing choice lists them.
